quote: 20. INDEMNIFICATION 20.1 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services.
rationale: Section 20 contains only a one-way Customer indemnity covering "every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services", with no Vendor indemnity for third-party IP infringement or misconduct anywhere in the Agreement (Section 9.3 even cross-refers to a non-existent Section 20.5 of infringement remedies). That is walk-away territory under INDEMN and fails the fallback outright. We therefore added a Vendor defence/indemnity at the preferred level (IP infringement of Services or Deliverables, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with notice, control-of-defence and cooperation, and narrowed our own indemnity to Customer-provided content and our breach of Applicable Law. We did not adopt the fallback 3x-annual-fees super-cap because Section 21.3 already treats indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims and volunteering a cap would weaken us; the dangling Section 20.5 reference in Section 9.3 pre-exists and should be conformed in the next turn.

verification.notes: Preferred checklist is complete: all four indemnity triggers (IP infringement of Services/Deliverables, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), the express defend obligation to Customer and Affiliates, the full notice/control/cooperation procedure, and the narrowed Customer indemnity are all present in operative text, not merely promised in the comment. Fallback is incomplete (no procure/modify/replace remedy, no refund fallback, no 3x annual Fees super-cap), but position-completeness only requires one level, and the preferred level is met. Declining the 3x super-cap is defensible on the record: Section 21.3 already carves indemnification obligations out of the liability cap as Excluded Claims, so volunteering a cap would be a customer-adverse extra and would itself risk a minimality failure. Minimality holds: the edit narrows Section 20.1 only to the two permitted Customer-indemnity triggers (required by element 10) and inserts a concise Vendor indemnity for a missing clause. No survival tail, at-own-expense wording, additional damages categories, or unrelated boilerplate was added, and no favourable existing language was deleted. Intent preserved: the Excluded Claims definition, the Fees carve-out in Section 21.3, and the Section 9.3 termination triggers all survive without contradiction. The dangling cross-reference in Section 9.3 to "Section 20.5" pre-dates the redline and is not created by it. Repair recommendations for the next turn (not defects in the checklist): (i) number the inserted paragraph (e.g., 20.2) so it is citable and so Section 9.3's reference to the infringement remedies can be conformed; (ii) if the Agreement does not define "Affiliate", change "Affiliates" to lowercase "affiliates" to avoid an undefined capitalised term; (iii) consider adding the Section 9.3 procure/modify/replace/refund remedies so the pre-existing cross-reference resolves — that would also close the fallback gaps at no cost.

quote: Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel.
rationale: The IP package sits at our preferred position. § 14.2 vests ownership of each Deliverable and work product in Customer and contains Vendor's express present assignment of all worldwide right, title, and interest (with personnel assignments and further-assurance support). § 14.3 limits Vendor's retained rights to Vendor Technology, which § 1.8 defines as Vendor's pre-existing technology and excludes Customer Data and Customer's pre-existing IP; where Vendor Technology is embedded in or needed to use a Deliverable, § 13.2 grants Customer and its Affiliates a "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence" to use, modify and create derivative works for Customer's business, satisfying the perpetual, irrevocable and royalty-free markers. § 14.1 confirms Customer owns all Customer Data and Customer-provided material and that no right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process it "solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer" — service delivery only, not independent exploitation — reinforced by § 15.1's bar on selling, advertising, data-combination or model-training uses. § 14.4 negates joint ownership absent a separately signed instrument identifying exploitation rights. Minor points noted but not flagged: ownership is expressed as "subject to payment of the applicable Fees," and § 14.4 leaves open a future opt-in to joint ownership by signed instrument. Separately, § 13.1's revocable, Customer-only Services licence is a licence-scope issue for the LICENSE rule and is not double-flagged here.

quote: 21.1 Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.
rationale: Section 21.1 caps both Parties at one month of "Fees actually paid" and applies "without exception", which (i) sits far below the fallback 12-months'-fees basis and below the 6-month walk-away floor, and (ii) overrides the Excluded Claims regime in 21.2-21.3, so indemnities, confidentiality, data-protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement all sit inside a one-month cap with no super-cap. Defined "Fees" (§1.5) also excludes taxes, expenses and implementation charges, narrowing the base further. Section 21.2 already gives a mutual exclusion of indirect and consequential damages, so the surgical fix is to correct the cap basis in 21.1, restore the Excluded Claims exception, and conform 21.3 so the payment carve-out reaches Customer's payment obligations generally rather than a subset of defined Fees.

verification.notes: Finding status "deviation" is correct: original 21.1 capped both Parties at one month of "Fees actually paid" — below the 6-month walk-away floor — and "without exception" nullified the Excluded Claims regime, placing indemnities, confidentiality, data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement inside a one-month cap with no super-cap. Preferred level is complete: mutual cap, greater-of twelve months' fees paid or payable measured to the claim plus USD 1,000,000 floor, retained mutual consequential-damages exclusion in 21.2, the full 21.3 Excluded Claims list operative again, and a payment carve-out reaching Customer's payment obligations generally. Minimality holds: only two surgical edits were made — replacing the cap basis and the "without exception" override in 21.1, and replacing the narrow "undisputed Fees for conforming Services" noun phrase in 21.3. The latter is required by the checklist element, since §1.5 "Fees" excludes taxes, expenses and implementation charges and so covers only a subset of Customer's payment obligations. No survival tails, procedures, expense language or extra damages categories were added, and 21.2 was left untouched. Watch-item (not a failure): the amended 21.3 also drops the "undisputed" and "conforming Services" qualifiers, which were Customer-favourable limits on an uncapped Customer payment exposure. The element could be met by a narrower edit such as "Customer's obligation to pay undisputed amounts due under this Agreement for conforming Services"; the margin comment already offers to restore those qualifiers, which is the safer negotiating stance. Intent preserved: 21.2's cross-reference to "Excluded Claims" and 21.3's definition remain coherent, the direct-damages sentence in 21.2 survives, and no undefined term or dangling reference is created (lower-case "fees" in 21.1 reads as the generic term and is the playbook's own formulation, though the drafter may confirm the intended base with the counterparty).

quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
rationale: Section 24 satisfies the preferred position. § 24.1 lets Customer assign without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all assets (notice is a Customer-friendly formality only). § 24.2 bars Vendor assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without Customer's prior written consent (not unreasonably withheld) and bars assignment to a direct Customer competitor. § 24.3 applies a mutual, reasonableness-qualified consent standard to other assignments, and § 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any termination, suspension, repricing, acceleration or service-reduction right on Customer's change of control. § 13.3 adds a Customer-only licence transfer right tied to permitted assignments. The only wording short of preferred is that the competitor bar in § 24.2 is framed as "without Customer's consent" rather than absolute — a minor sub-element within our own control, noted rather than redlined. No provision binds Customer asymmetrically or gives Vendor a change-of-control exit, so there is nothing to flag.

quote: Customer owes Fees only for conforming Services provided through the effective termination date, and Vendor shall promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the period after that date.
rationale: The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, or early-termination/minimum-fee obligation payable by Customer. Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "termination fee", "shortfall", and every termination and fee provision (§§ 6.2, 7.1–7.5, 9.1–9.5, 10.1–10.2, 21.1–21.4, 22.2, 27.3) return no Customer-payable liquidated amount. To the contrary, § 9.4 gives Customer a convenience-termination right under which it "owes Fees only for conforming Services provided through the effective termination date" with a refund of prepaid Fees, § 27.3 allows force-majeure termination "without penalty", and § 7.1 bars unstated minimum-use or similar charges. This meets the preferred position (Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties), so no redline is proposed. The § 2.1 take-or-pay minimum commitment is a volume commitment rather than a liquidated damages or penalty mechanic and is addressed under the minimum-commitment rule; we do not flag it twice here. The only Customer payment triggered by a shortfall (§ 22.2 audit underpayment) is payment of amounts actually owed plus audit costs, not a liquidated sum.

rationale: Section 18 meets our preferred insurance position in full: CGL of USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, professional errors and omissions of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability of USD 5,000,000 (granted unconditionally, so the "where Vendor processes Customer Data" trigger is satisfied a fortiori). Section 18.2 obliges Vendor to provide certificates of insurance on request, and adds Customer-favourable extras (primary coverage, notice of cancellation, and confirmation that insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities). Employer's liability of USD 1,000,000 is additional cover beyond our checklist and is not adverse. No redline required.
